title: Foundations quiz
intro: Six questions on the ideas behind cases 01 to 04. You'll see right away whether each answer is right and why. No tutor, no time limit.

questions.title: Too many urgent tickets
questions.prompt: This query should list urgent tickets that are open or pending. It returns far too many rows. Which line has the bug?
questions.explain: SQL handles AND before OR, so line 4 reads as "(urgent and open) or pending". Every pending ticket gets in, urgent or not. Use `status IN ('open', 'pending')`, or wrap the OR in parentheses.

questions.title: The date that became a number
questions.prompt: `date_diff('day', created_at, 2026-10-01)` fails with an error saying it got an INTEGER. Why?
options: Without quotes, SQL reads 2026-10-01 as subtraction: 2026 minus 10 minus 1.
date_diff only works on timestamps, not dates.
Dates have to be written as 10/01/2026.
created_at has to come last in date_diff.
questions.explain: Unquoted, `2026-10-01` is math and equals 2015. Write `DATE '2026-10-01'`: the quotes make it text, and `DATE` tells SQL to read the text as a date.

questions.title: Clean the categories
questions.prompt: This query should list each distinct category after cleaning: lowercase, with '-issue' removed, and spaces trimmed. It doesn't run. Fix it in the editor and press Run.
questions.broken:
SELECT DISTINCT replace(category, '-issue', '') AND lower(category) AND trim(category) AS clean
FROM tickets;
questions.explain: AND combines true/false conditions; it can't chain text functions. To apply several functions to one value, put each inside the next: `trim(lower(replace(category, '-issue', '')))`. The innermost one runs first.

questions.title: What survives the filter?
questions.prompt: A category column holds three values: 'Billing', a single space ' ', and NULL. Which rows does this keep?
questions.code:
SELECT category
FROM t
WHERE trim(category) <> ''
questions.explain: `trim(' ')` becomes empty text, which equals '', so the space is dropped. NULL is dropped too: comparing NULL to anything gives "unknown", and WHERE only keeps rows that are true.

questions.title: Three orgs, one customer
questions.prompt: The orgs table has org 1 (crm_customer_id C-101), org 2 (C-999) and org 3 (blank). The customers table has only C-101. What does this return?
questions.code:
SELECT o.org_id, c.customer_id
FROM orgs o
LEFT JOIN customers c
  ON c.customer_id = o.crm_customer_id
questions.explain: A LEFT JOIN keeps every org. Org 1 finds its customer. Orgs 2 and 3 find no partner, so the customer side comes back NULL. Filtering for that NULL is how you find the unmatched ones.

questions.title: The orgs that hid
questions.prompt: This query should find helpdesk orgs with no matching CRM customer. It finds the orgs with a blank ID but misses the ones with a mistyped ID. Which line has the bug?
questions.explain: ON describes which rows belong together, so it needs `=`. With `!=`, an org with a mistyped ID "matches" every customer, so its customer side is never NULL and WHERE skips it. Find non-matches afterward, with `IS NULL`.
